rows.label: Black Hat
rows.value: No authorisation. Malicious or self-interested intent. Criminal in all jurisdictions. Goal: financial gain, disruption, espionage, or ideological impact.

rows.label: White Hat
rows.value: Full written authorisation (PSP framework). Defined scope. Documented findings. Professional context. Legal and ethical. Goal: improve security for the client.

rows.label: Grey Hat
rows.value: No authorisation. Benign intent. Still criminal under CFAA and Computer Misuse Act. Good intentions are not a legal defence. Do not operate here.

rows.label: CFAA (US)
rows.value: Criminalises accessing a computer without authorisation or exceeding authorised access. No damage required. No data theft required. No malicious intent required. Federal offence.

rows.label: Computer Misuse Act (UK)
rows.value: Three offences: (1) unauthorised access, (2) unauthorised access with intent to commit further offences, (3) unauthorised modification. Intent only determines the charge level, not guilt.

rows.label: IT Act 2000 (India)
rows.value: Section 66 criminalises dishonestly or fraudulently accessing any computer resource without authorisation. Penalties include imprisonment up to 3 years.

rows.label: Responsible Disclosure
rows.value: Notify vendor privately → 90-day countdown → patch released → publish. Professional standard. Protects users. Protects researcher. Builds relationships.

rows.label: Full Disclosure
rows.value: Publish immediately, no vendor notification. Maximum pressure on vendor. Immediate risk to users. Elevated legal risk for researcher. Use as last resort.

rows.label: Bug Bounty + Safe Harbour
rows.value: Formal programme with written authorisation, defined scope, financial rewards, and safe harbour clause. The safest framework for independent security research.

rows.label: Before testing
rows.value: Confirm the target has a bug bounty programme OR a published VDP with safe harbour. Confirm your target is in scope. Read every rule.

rows.label: During testing
rows.value: Access only your own accounts. Collect the minimum data needed to prove the flaw. Document everything with timestamps.

rows.label: After finding
rows.value: Contact vendor privately. Do not share details with anyone. Set a 90-day timer. Keep records of all communication.

rows.label: After 90 days
rows.value: If no patch: publish regardless. If patch released: coordinate disclosure timeline with vendor and publish together.
